title: Ge/ZnS Dual-Cavity Dual-Band Bandpass Filter on CaF2
scientific_hypothesis: Germanium (high-index) and Zinc Sulfide (low-index) form a viable material pair for mid-IR dual-band bandpass filters on CaF2 substrate, achieving high transmission in 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm bands while blocking 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm, with 22 total layers in a dual-cavity topology.
design_principle: Dual-cavity bandpass filter constructed from alternating high/low index quarter-wave stacks, with two resonance cavities tuned to methane and CO2 absorption bands respectively. Ge provides high index contrast (~4.0 vs ~2.3) for sharp spectral edges.
proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Ge cavity | [Ge/ZnS]_3 | ZnS cavity | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | CaF2 substrate. Total 22 finite layers: 5+5=10 mirror layers, 3+3=6 mirror layers, 2 cavity layers, plus 4 transition layers = 22 layers exact.
design_variables: Cavity layer positions fixed at layers 11 and 17
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional PVD-depositable IR materials
Thickness bounds [100, 500] nm ensure deposition feasibility
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack principle for bandpass filters
Ge/ZnS index contrast suitable for mid-IR
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS pair has documented mid-IR transparency unlike Si/SiO2
Higher index contrast than Si/SiO2 enables sharper band edges
22 layers provides sufficient blocking while staying under 24-layer limit
known_risks: Ge may exhibit absorption features in mid-IR requiring verification
Thermal stress between Ge and ZnS during deposition
Cavity coupling may produce unwanted spectral ripple
execution_request_english: Using Transfer Matrix Method, optimize a 22-layer dielectric stack on CaF2 substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Layer sequence: Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS. Initialize all thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness at 3300 nm center wavelength. Set thickness optimization bounds [100, 500] nm for all layers. Evaluate transmittance across four bands: 2500-3100 nm (suppress), 3250-3350 nm (transmit), 4200-4300 nm (transmit), 4450-5000 nm (suppress). Use Ge and ZnS as dielectric materials with CaF2 substrate. No metal layers allowed. Total layer count fixed at 22. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Changed material system from Si/SiO2 to Ge/ZnS to address material_data failure. Si/SiO2 has absorption issues in mid-IR range; Ge/ZnS is documented for mid-IR bandpass applications. Preserved dual-cavity topology and 22-layer count from route_02.
